Dependencies must point inward:

- Domain depends on no other application project.
- Application depends on Domain.
- Infrastructure depends on Application and Domain.
- Api depends on Application and may reference Infrastructure only as required for composition and dependency registration.
- Inner layers never depend on outer layers; Domain and Application never reference Infrastructure-specific types.

If a feature seems to need an outward reference, reconsider the abstraction boundary instead of adding the reference.

| Layer (`1-architecture/backend-layers.md`) | Project |
|---|---|
| Domain | `backend/<Name>.Domain/` |
| Application | `backend/<Name>.Application/` |
| Infrastructure | `backend/<Name>.Infrastructure/` |
| Api | `backend/<Name>.Api/` (contains `Program.cs`) |

`ProjectReference` entries implement the Level 1 dependency direction; the project hook rejects outward references (Domain → any layer, Application → Infrastructure/Api, Infrastructure → Api).

- Never weaken, delete, skip, or suppress relevant tests or compiler, TypeScript, lint, or analyzer failures merely to make verification pass — no strong-to-weak assertion swaps, no deleting an inconvenient failing test.
- Preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing; stop when progress has clearly stalled rather than making speculative edits.

Never fix a dependency problem with an invalid project reference (for example Application → Infrastructure); re-read `.claude/rules/1-architecture/backend-layers.md`.

A green build obtained by violating the architecture (outward references, persistence types in Application, business logic in Controllers, Angular-only authorization, HTTP calls scattered into components) is not a successful repair. Behavior established with a temporary probe during diagnosis is preserved as `verify` step 4 requires.

Check the changed code against the Level 1 rules (`backend-layers.md`, `persistence-boundary.md`, `entry-points.md`, `outcomes.md`) and their Level 2 bindings: Domain independence, Application free of Infrastructure and persistence-framework types, thin entry points, Application Services orchestrating use cases, specific repository abstractions, the Unit of Work as commit boundary. Also check proportionality: abstraction count justified by actual complexity, and no consequential pattern without approval. Never report a violation merely because the code differs from a pattern this architecture has not adopted (`1-architecture/overview.md`).

Add only the references `layout.md` maps from the Level 1 dependency direction, as `<ProjectReference>` items in the project files (for example `<ProjectReference Include="..\<Name>.Domain\<Name>.Domain.csproj" />` in `<Name>.Application.csproj`). Never add an outward reference to make compilation easier. The project hook blocks `dotnet add/remove … reference` and `dotnet reference add/remove` (reference-graph changes: CLAUDE.md → Decision control), reports every reference change, and rejects outward references — include those reports in the scaffolding report.

1. Confirm a new assembly is justified — a new production project or layer is Reserved (CLAUDE.md → Decision control).
2. Identify its responsibility; add only the minimum references, preserving dependency direction.
3. Update shared build/package configuration when necessary; build and test the affected solution.

The physical structure matches the requested scope; references respect the architecture; the approved stack is used; no unnecessary projects or speculative directories exist; backend and frontend (when present) build; relevant tests pass; local Development configuration is usable; nothing unrelated was reorganized.

- **Architecture** — when the change touches boundaries, re-read and check the owning rules: project references and dependency direction (`1-architecture/backend-layers.md`), repository and Unit of Work boundary (`persistence-boundary.md`), entry points (`entry-points.md`). When a Domain or persistence change affects seeded entities, confirm the seeder was updated and stays valid for a freshly recreated Development database (`3-project/data-lifecycle.md`) and that new migrations were reviewed (`development-workflow` → Co-changes).
- **Formatting and analyzers** — when configured, for example `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`; do not add a formatter or analyzer dependency just to verify. Analyzer output is evidence that still needs context.

After all fixes, review the final diff again for: accidental unrelated edits; commented-out code; temporary logging; unintended TODO/FIXME markers; stale temporary tests or scripts; architecture drift; unapproved drift from `SPECIFICATION.md` or `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md`; stale code, tests, docs, or configuration after a `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md` change; behavior verified manually but never preserved as a test.

canonical_policy.name: Domain is infrastructure independent
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Keep Domain independent of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Framework/transport independence, practical persistence-config preference and Docker-concern exclusion are explicit. No universal example-specific entity mapping inferred.

context_quotes:
- Domain must stay independent of persistence frameworks, web/transport frameworks, HTTP, persistence, and external-service implementation concerns.
- Simple domain entities are the default. For CRUD-oriented applications and straightforward workflows, keep entities simple and enforce use-case and workflow rules in Application Services (default). Validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions, or allowed/forbidden edits do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

- `DbContext`, `DbSet<T>`, EF Core APIs and LINQ-to-EF expressions, EF attributes and mapping types, and SQL Server provider types are persistence-framework types for the purposes of the Level 1 boundary rules.
- Entity mappings live in Infrastructure as `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes, keeping persistence configuration out of Domain entities where practical (prefer).
- The Infrastructure implementation of `IUnitOfWork` delegates to the same scoped `DbContext` that the use case's repositories share.
